summary: Jean-François Desgranges was an Indologist who studied at the École Normale (École Normale Supérieure) in 1795 and under Antoine-Léonard Chézy.

An archaeologist, historian, and Indologist, Jean-François Jarrige studied at Lycée Claude Fauriel, École du Louvre, and the University of Paris. He served at the Guimet Museum as director from 1986 to 2004 and head until circa 2008.

Philosopher Jean-François Lyotard studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, Paris Nanterre University, and the University of Paris. His academic appointments included posts at the University of Paris, Paris Nanterre, Paris 8 Vincennes-Saint-Denis, UC Irvine, and Emory University.
Jean-François Revel was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Jean-Baptiste-Say, Lycée du Parc, and the École Normale Supérieure in 1943.

Jean-Jacques Bochinger was a scholar of religion and Indology. He studied at the universities of Strasbourg, Heidelberg, and Göttingen, and under Eugène Burnouf, later serving as minister at the University of Strasbourg in 1830.

Jean-Jacques-Antoine Ampère was a historian, archaeologist, and linguist who studied at Lycée Henri-IV and under Eugène Burnouf. He held posts at the Athénée de Marseille, the Sorbonne, the École Normale Supérieure, and the Collège de France.

Linguist Jean-Louis Burnouf studied under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He held professorships at Lycée Charlemagne, Lycée Louis-le-Grand, and Collège de France (1817–1844), later serving as chief librarian at the University of Paris and Sorbonne in 1840.

Jean-Luc Achard is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and was affiliated with the Centre national de la recherche scientifique (attested 2003–2004).

Jean-Luc Chevillard is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Antoine Culioli, later working as a CNRS researcher from circa 1993 and as a lecturer at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Jean-Marie Casal was an archaeologist who studied at the Musée du Louvre under Philippe Stern. He served with the Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan (1951–1958), Musées Nationaux (1957), and the National Centre for Scientific Research (1969–1975).

Jean-Noël Robert is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who studied under Bernard Frank. His career includes posts at CNRS, École Pratique des Hautes Études, Institut des hautes études japonaises, and a professorship at the Collège de France (2011–2022).

Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat was a sinologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held the Chair for Chinese at the Collège de France (1814–1832) and served as president of the Société Asiatique.

Jean-Pierre Drège is a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Burgundy, INALCO, and under Yves Hervouet. He served as president of the École française d'Extrême-Orient from circa 1998 to 2004.

Jean-Pierre de Menasce was an Iranian and religious studies scholar. Educated at Balliol College, the Sorbonne, and under Émile Benveniste, he taught at the University of Fribourg (circa 1938–1948) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1949–1970).
Jean-Pierre-Guillaume Pauthier was a scholar of sinology and Indology who studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat and Antoine-Léonard Chézy between circa 1823 and 1832.
Jean-Sylvain Bailly was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the French Academy of Sciences and became a member of the Académie Française in 1763.

Indologist Jeannette M. van Gelder studied at Leiden University and Utrecht University under Jacob Samuel Speyer, Jean Philippe Vogel, Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck, and Willem Caland. She later served as a librarian at the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences.

Jeannine Auboyer was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the École du Louvre and EPHE. She served as chief curator at the Guimet Museum (1965–1980) and held a chair at the École du Louvre (1965–1980).

Jeff Dolven studied at Oxford and Yale University. He held posts at Harvard University and Brandeis University before becoming a professor of English at Princeton University circa 2001, and a fellow at Trinity College, Cambridge (circa 2017–2018).

Philosopher Jeff Malpas studied at the University of Auckland and Australian National University. He held positions at the University of New England and Murdoch University before joining the University of Tasmania, where he became Professor in 1999 and Emeritus Distinguished Professor in 2018.
